message.subject: Re: Price gone up from £90 to £112?
message.body:
Hi Lauren,

Thanks for explaining. Can I ask who I would write to if I wanted to make a formal complaint about this? I never got any reminder that it needed doing, and nobody told me before taking the extra £22, which is a lot for me this month. I've uploaded the letter now.

Amelia

thread.body:
Hello,

I've just been looking at my bank statement and noticed my payment on 8 September was £112.00. Every other month it's been £90.00 (August was £90.00, for example). I haven't changed anything on my plan and I don't remember getting an email about a price rise, unless I missed it?

I'm still on Universal Credit so I thought I was on the reduced price. Could you let me know why it's gone up and whether I'll be paying £112 from now on? It's quite a jump for me.

Thank you,
Amelia Hughes

Hi Amelia,

Thanks for getting in touch. Your concession was due to be re-verified on 1 September 2026, and as it wasn't re-verified in time, the standard price of £112.00 applied from your 8 September charge. You can re-verify by uploading your Universal Credit letter under Billing in your account. The concession price then returns from the next billing date after it is verified.

Lauren

policy.label: Policy P5.4: Prices, price changes and concessions
policy.text:
Monthly plan prices. United Kingdom: one product £112, two products £164; concession £90 and £131.

Price changes. We give at least 30 days' notice by email. A new price applies from the first billing date on or after the date it takes effect.

Concessions. About 20% off for holders of an Australian Pensioner Concession Card or Health Care Card, a New Zealand Community Services Card, or, in the UK, proof of a means-tested benefit such as Universal Credit. A concession is verified when it is added and re-verified every 12 months; we email a reminder 30 days before it is due. If it is not re-verified in time, the standard price applies from the next billing date, and the concession price returns from the next billing date after it is verified again. Patients re-verify by uploading their card or letter under Billing in their account. A new concession is added the same way, and the concession price applies from the next billing date after it is verified.

A change to the products on a plan changes the price from the next billing date. There is no referral programme and there are no discount codes.

policy.label: Policy P2.2: Talking to a person and complaints
policy.text:
A patient can always talk to a person. Offer a call back at a time they choose, within 1 business day, or live chat during support hours. When a patient asks for a person, a team member writes the reply; there is no automated reply. Never make a patient ask twice, and never send them back to a help article instead.

Complaints: acknowledge within 1 business day, give the patient the name of the person who owns the complaint, and aim to resolve it within 10 business days. The team lead reviews every complaint. Complaints about clinical care go to the clinical lead, and complaints about privacy go to the privacy officer. If we cannot resolve a complaint, tell the patient how to contact the independent health complaints body in their country.

policy.label: Policy P3.2: Renewals and follow-up consults
policy.text:
Each prescription covers a set number of monthly repeats. While a patient is on a plan they have a follow-up consult every 3 months, included in the plan price. When the repeats are about to run out, they need a renewal consult. We email a reminder 21 days before the last repeat is used. A renewal can be done at a booked follow-up if it falls before the next billing date.

Patients should book a renewal consult at least 7 days before their next billing date. If the new prescription is not approved by the billing date, we hold the plan charge and the order waits in script pending; we charge once the prescription is approved, so nobody pays for an order that cannot be sent. Renewal consults on an active plan cost nothing extra. A patient whose plan was cancelled for less than 6 months can restart on their existing prescription if it still has repeats; otherwise they need a new consult.

Agents can book and explain renewals. Only a clinician decides whether to renew a prescription and what is prescribed.

A complaint goes to a person: acknowledge within 1 business day, name the owner, team lead review, and, if it cannot be resolved, how to reach the independent health complaints body. No AI draft. Her uploaded letter can be checked alongside: the concession returns from the next billing date after it is verified.
